items.title: Ultrasound Physics Interactive Modules
items.scope: Seven visual modules: pressure/amplitude, power versus pressure, intensity and beam area, decibels, tissue attenuation, interference, and spatial/temporal resolution.
items.recommendation: Best starting point for understanding ultrasound relationships: each concept has its own interactive visual tool.

items.title: Renal Osteodystrophy: The Complete Loop
items.scope: Simulates the kidney–vitamin D–gut–calcium–phosphate–PTH–bone feedback loop, including loss of kidney function.
items.recommendation: A focused visual explanation of a causal mechanism that is easy to memorize without understanding.

items.title: QC Orbit Academy
items.scope: Ten briefing lessons plus interval sorting and high-yield rules for nuclear medicine, CT, mammography, MRI, ultrasound, dose calibrators, artifacts, and current versus legacy QC wording.
items.recommendation: Combines explanations with retrieval practice; especially useful for learning QC intervals and remembering why tests exist.

items.title: Radiology Teaching Points Review
items.scope: Seventeen sections on PCA/thalamic territories, infarct localization and hemorrhage, DWI/ADC pitfalls, CAA, Heidelberg classification, chronic infarction/CLOCC, cervical trauma, cord injury, spine interpretation, stenosis grading, and reporting.
coverage: I. Posterior cerebral artery anatomy and infarct territories
II. Occipital, temporal, and parietal lobe localization
III. Hemorrhage associated with a PCA-territory infarct
IV. Diffusion restriction, DWI, ADC, and T2 blackout
V. Cerebral amyloid angiopathy as a differential consideration
VI. Hemorrhagic transformation terminology and Heidelberg classification
VII. Chronic infarction, cortical laminar necrosis, and enhancement
VIII. Splenium of the corpus callosum: PCA infarct versus CLOCC
IX. Cervical spine trauma: degenerative change versus occult injury
X. Traumatic cord contusion without fracture
XI. Efficient cervical spine MRI interpretation workflow
XII. Using CT to characterize degenerative cervical disease
XV. What “severe” should mean across spine stenosis systems

items.title: Liver Imaging Teaching Points Review
items.scope: CT steatosis, chemical-shift MRI/iron, ascites anatomy, varices, cysts, hemangioma, abscess, FNH, indeterminate liver lesions, enhancement bins, reporting, biopsy, and management. The source notes a gap between its two lecture files.
items.recommendation: A deeper companion to the liver-lesion workflow, connecting imaging appearance, differential diagnosis, uncertainty, and reporting.
coverage: II. In-phase and opposed-phase MRI in the presence of ascites and iron
III. Peritoneal and retroperitoneal anatomy demonstrated by ascites
V. Fundamental philosophy for focal liver lesions
VI. Hepatic cysts and cystic lesions
X. Differential diagnosis of an indeterminate lesion
XIII. Report lesion size and change
XV. Biopsy of a possible hemangioma
XVI. MRI after an ambiguous multiphase CT

items.title: Soft Tissue Lecture Lab

items.recommendation: Figure-specific observations, interpretations, pitfalls, and recall questions connect a systematic approach to actual imaging examples.

audit.method: Reviewed accessible repository inventories, all 32,018 The-Library tree entries, app page sources, organized quiz titles, relevant standalone source files, and Sites metadata/version provenance. AI primer source was also inspected. Existing links only; no apps were copied or recreated.
audit.limits: Snapshot, not automatic synchronization. Not every underlying lesson, personal record, clinical statement, or app runtime was tested. Suggested usefulness is an editorial judgment based on content structure and study features, not measured learning outcomes. Source-only tools may need local/server setup. Private Sites retain their existing access requirements.
audit.duplicates: Organized Core Review paths are primary; legacy top-level routes are alternate links. Educational Emporium copies and redirected image galleries are grouped with the corresponding resource. Individual chapters and modules are counted as resources, not separate apps.
audit.publicLinkResult: All 243 checked public app/alias links returned HTTP 200 on 2026-10-22. This checks entry-link availability, not all underlying app behavior. Private Sites and server/source entries were not runtime-tested.

editDates.method: GitHub dates use committer timestamps from the newest commit touching each resource folder (including scripts, banks, styles and assets), an individual standalone HTML file, or the whole repository for repository-level entries. Sites dates use the source commit referenced by the latest saved version. These are recorded source edits, not local file modification times, study activity, or the catalog entry date.
editDates.limits: Folder/repository metrics can include content imports, generated assets, progress files, moves or maintenance. Group launchers include descendant edits. Alternate links retain the primary resource date. Unsaved local changes and live database edits are outside this metric. Dates are a refreshable snapshot; unknown dates sort last.
